purpose: Single source of truth for player-facing realism authorities and their intended release toggles. Current development activation remains separately gated until native acceptance.

internalCore.reason: Lifecycle, serialization and shared utility substrate; it must not itself impose gameplay effects.

modules.disableContract: Disabling body stops new body progression and body-derived penalties without deleting saved state. Re-enable resumes from retained state under an explicit migration/version policy.

Combat must fall back safely when injury is disabled. No bleeding, impairment or treatment listener may remain half-active. Existing injury state is retained but must not continue applying penalties while disabled.
When disabled, realpass must not rewrite native damage or create wounds. Vanilla/authored combat behavior remains authoritative.
When disabled, realpass adds no physical armor interception or armor wear. Ordinary clothing never becomes ballistic armor merely because the armor module is disabled.
When disabled, realpass does not add structural/physiological cyberware consequences. It must not become a generic cyberware balance module.
Disabling presentation removes realpass-specific presentation without changing simulation state or disabling useful native scanner/quickhack functionality.
Off by default. No background watcher, logger, recorder, scheduled task or helper service may remain when diagnostics are disabled.

releaseRules: One realpass settings surface owns public toggles.
A source-mod setting is not automatically a realpass feature.
Every retained gameplay feature maps to exactly one owning realpass module.
Disabling one module must not require disabling unrelated modules.
Presentation may read simulation state but must not become a simulation authority.
Out-of-scope inherited features are removed from the distributed runtime rather than merely hidden behind disabled defaults.
Development activation gates stay closed until the corresponding native acceptance gate is satisfied.
